h: Outdoor City by Day, Games City by Night
p: Sheffield likes to call itself the Outdoor City, and with a third of the city inside the Peak District National Park, it's earned the title. Plenty of visitors spend the day climbing, cycling or walking in the hills before coming back into town for the evening. If that sounds like your plan, a games bar is the ideal way to round things off without anyone needing a dress code.

Getting into the centre from the station is a short walk up past Sheaf Square, a striking spot with its stainless steel water feature, a nod to the city's industrial past. Supertram links the centre with Meadowhall, Hillsborough and the suburbs, and buses cover the rest. If you're coming from the Peak District, the trains from the Hope Valley line get you into the city quickly.

For larger groups, the usual advice applies: book early, mix your teams and agree on prizes before you start. If you're coming off a day in the hills, it might be worth booking food too, because you'll be starving by the time you get back. And don't worry about arriving in walking boots, though you may want to change before the photos.

For more city ideas, Kelham Island is a former industrial area full of craft breweries, pubs and restaurants, and its museum tells the story of Sheffield's steel heritage. The Botanical Gardens, a short way out of the centre, are a lovely spot on a sunny day, with Victorian glass pavilions and colourful borders. And the Crucible, home of the World Snooker Championship each spring, is a must-see for snooker fans.
